name: strategy-eval
description: Is an external strategy worth backtesting on a given market? Adversarial: the market is efficient and fee-eaten by default; a claim earns a probe only by surviving mechanism, fit, evidence, economics, scalability, access, and testability. Output is triage (worth a backtest + the exact probe), never 'implement'.

points.name: Mechanism validity
points.description: What is the edge and does it survive our reality — measured net of fees, out-of-sample, not gross/in-sample?

sub_points.name: Edge measured after fees, not gross
Out-of-sample, not in-sample (Brier-only = WEAK, not proof)

points.name: Market fit / preconditions
points.description: Does this market have the regime the edge needs?

sub_points.name: FLB needs a favorite/longshot regime; Benter needs a model that beats naive priors (weather yes, BTC no); arb needs an equivalent 2nd-venue contract
Is the naive YES-longshot flow the edge feeds on actually present?

points.name: Our internal evidence
points.description: What do our own paper/live trades say for THIS market?

points.name: Fee & adverse-selection economics
points.description: Does the edge clear fees and survive toxic flow?

sub_points.name: Single-name toxicity, ~33% return SD, one-sided-flow / inventory risk

points.name: Scalability
points.description: How many contracts can this absorb, and how far does that scale?

sub_points.name: Edge degrades with size (larger maker posts less-advantageous prices)
Realistic max contracts/day + scaling PATH (deepen vs add-markets) + proxy-vs-measured flag

points.name: Access / regulatory
points.description: Can a US person trade it via a real API?

sub_points.name: Venue access, geoblock (Polymarket NEVER circumvented), US-person, API

points.name: Testability
points.description: Can we actually run the probe cheaply?

sub_points.name: Do we have or can we cheaply get the data?
